text:
Maya: heads-up: found an auth parity issue between SDK and direct REST that is causing audit mismatch during onboarding. SDK auto-refreshes OAuth tokens on 401 and retries the request, but the server audit shows the successful operation under the refreshed service-token, not the original user token -> security team flagged it.

Evan: that's concerning. can you paste a minimal repro and which sdk version?

Maya: repro (node, sdk@2.8.0):
```js
// using a short-lived user token
await client.routes.create({ routeId: 'onboard-abcd' })
// when token expired, SDK logs show: 401 -> refresh token flow -> retry -> 200
```

Maya: curl sequence (manual):
```bash
# 1) expired token -> 401
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer user-expired" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/routes" -d '{"routeId":"onboard-abcd"}'
# -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# 2) refresh token with /oauth/token (explicit by client) -> get new user token -> retry
# 3) POST with new user token -> 200
```

Maya: with SDK it's different: server audit shows the successful create attributed to the SDK's internal service account token (service-rotate-xyz) instead of the refreshed user token. logs in staging: 
```
[2026-03-14T10:01:02Z] POST /v1/routes -> 401 (token expired)
[2026-03-14T10:01:02Z] SDK auth refresh: requesting new token from /internal/refresh -> got token service-rotate-xyz
[2026-03-14T10:01:03Z] RETRY POST /v1/routes -> 200 (actor=service-rotate-xyz)
```

Lina: wait, why is the SDK using a service token for refresh? the refresh call should mint a user-scoped token and the retried request should include that identity. if the SDK exposes a refresh hook (so apps can supply their own refresh callback) maybe it's misconfigured.

Evan: could be two things: 1) SDK falls back to an internal app-level refresh path when user refresh fails, 2) middleware swapped auth header incorrectly when retrying. both would cause audit to blame service account.

Jamie: this is a big DX & security problem. we should not lose original actor identity in server logs. proposed fixes: 1) SDK must preserve the identity chain and attach a header like X-Original-Actor when it must fall back, 2) never retry under a different principal without explicit opt-in, 3) surface an event/callback when token refresh/auto-retry happens so apps can log/decide.

Maya: agreed. sample-app's onboarding workflow relies on user identity for auditing and product entitlements. when audit shows service account did the create, it's impossible to reconcile who initiated the onboarding. security raised a ticket.

Evan: quick workaround in sample-app: disable SDK auto-refresh and handle token refresh explicitly in caller code (we do manual refresh and then re-call SDK with new token). but that defeats convenience.

Lina: reproduction details: staging logs show token refresh endpoint `/internal/refresh` returns a short-lived token tied to a service key when the upstream identity provider is unreachable. SDK took that and retried. we should at least propagate original error if the refresh doesn't yield a user token.

Jamie: I'll draft RED-6130: "SDK: preserve original actor identity on auth refresh / don't retry under different principal" and a PR. Immediate plan: change SDK to 1) expose a configurable `onAuthRefresh` callback which receives { originalToken, refreshResult }, 2) by default do not retry if refresh yields a non-user/service-mismatched token; instead surface an auth error to caller, 3) if caller opts into automatic fallback to service-token, SDK must include X-Original-Actor header in retried requests. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/pull/1401 (WIP).

auth-bot: Created issue RED-6130: "SDK auth refresh should not obscure original actor in audit logs" assigned to @Jamie. Priority: P0.

Maya: please also add telemetry: emit a log line when SDK performs auto-refresh and include the token type (user|service) and whether it retried. we need this in observability to triage quickly.

Jamie: yes. add response metadata `auth_refresh: { attempted: true, result: 'user'|'service'|'failed' }` and make it available on response.raw. Also add a debug flag to log stack for token refresh attempts.

Evan: add unit tests simulating provider down and ensure SDK does not silently retry as service. integration test should assert server audit retains original actor if a refresh succeeded for the user.

Lina: I'll help with test harness for simulating refresh endpoint returning service token vs user token. also audit other SDKs for same behavior (py/go).

Maya: sample-app patch to disable auto-refresh pushed to branch onboarding/auth-safety; will monitor. thanks team. :thumbsup:

Jamie: plan: ship patch 2.8.1 with opt-out behavior and callback, full behavior change in 2.9.0 with telemetry. Migration note & security advisory to customer-facing teams. ETA: 24 hours for patch.

Maya: thanks. ping @security and @platform teams for visibility.

auth-bot: Linked RED-6130 to security advisory draft SD-22 and alerted #security.
